title: Clean up a messy lead list
goal: You will merge duplicate leads, correct their owners, and create a focused list view for ongoing lead cleanup.
prerequisites: Read and edit access to Leads
Delete permission on Leads for merging
Active duplicate rules in the Salesforce org

steps.action: Select the All Open Leads list view.
steps.where: Leads tab, list view dropdown beside the current list view name.
steps.why: A shared open-lead list gives you a broad starting set for cleanup.
steps.checkpoint: The list view heading reads "All Open Leads" and open lead rows appear.
hint_levels: Start with the dropdown above the lead table.
Choose the view that includes open leads across owners.
Click Leads > list view dropdown > All Open Leads.

steps.action: Open a lead showing a potential-duplicates alert.
steps.where: Lead list table, lead-name link, then the Potential Duplicates component on the record page.
steps.why: Salesforce exposes matches identified by your org's active duplicate rules on the record.
steps.checkpoint: The lead record displays a Potential Duplicates card reporting at least one possible match.
hint_levels: Look for a lead that Salesforce has flagged.
Open its record and locate the Potential Duplicates card, commonly in the right column.
Click the lead name, then find Potential Duplicates on the record page.

steps.action: Open the duplicate comparison for that lead.
steps.why: The comparison lets you confirm that the records represent the same person before merging.
steps.checkpoint: A comparison window lists the suspected lead records and their field values.
hint_levels: Use the action inside the duplicate warning.
The Potential Duplicates card contains the control that opens matching records.
In Potential Duplicates, click View Duplicates.

steps.action: Merge the confirmed duplicate records while choosing the most complete record as the master.
steps.where: Duplicate comparison window, record selection controls, "Next," field-value selectors, and "Merge Leads" button.
steps.why: The master survives while selected values and related activity are consolidated into it.
steps.checkpoint: Salesforce returns to one lead record and shows a successful-merge confirmation.
hint_levels: Keep the record with the strongest data and history.
Select only true duplicates, continue, then choose the winning value for each conflicting field.
Select the duplicate leads > click Next > select the master and preferred field values > click Merge Leads > confirm.

steps.action: Repeat the duplicate review and merge for every remaining flagged lead in the cleanup set.
steps.where: Leads tab and each flagged lead's Potential Duplicates component.
steps.why: Clearing all reviewed duplicate groups leaves one usable record per person.
steps.checkpoint: Every reviewed lead either has no Potential Duplicates warning or contains matches you intentionally left separate.
hint_levels: Work through the remaining alerts using the same test.
Compare identity fields such as email, phone, name, and company before each merge.
Return to Leads > open the next flagged lead > View Duplicates > compare > merge only confirmed matches.

steps.action: Select the leads that should be assigned to the same correct owner.
steps.where: Leads list view table, row checkboxes beside the lead names.
steps.why: Selecting a verified group allows one controlled ownership update.
steps.checkpoint: The intended rows are checked and the list-view action bar is visible.
hint_levels: Group only records that belong to one owner.
Use the checkbox column and verify the current Owner values before proceeding.
On Leads > All Open Leads, check each applicable row in the leftmost column.

steps.action: Transfer the selected leads to their correct owner.
steps.where: List-view action bar, "Change Owner" button, owner lookup, and "Submit" button.
steps.why: Correct ownership restores accountability and accurate work queues.
steps.checkpoint: The selected rows show the new name in the Lead Owner column after the list refreshes.
hint_levels: Use the ownership action above the selected rows.
Choose Change Owner, search for the user or queue, and decide whether notification is needed.
Click Change Owner > search and select the owner > optionally select Send email notification > click Submit.

steps.action: Create a list view named "Lead Cleanup Queue".
steps.where: Leads tab, List View Controls gear menu, "New" dialog.
steps.why: A dedicated view makes future hygiene checks repeatable.
steps.checkpoint: The list view heading reads "Lead Cleanup Queue" above the lead table.
hint_levels: The list-management menu sits above the table.
Create a new view and make it visible to the people responsible for cleanup.
Click List View Controls > New > enter Lead Cleanup Queue > choose visibility > Save.

steps.action: Filter the cleanup view to show all open leads created or modified within your team's review window.
steps.where: Lead Cleanup Queue, Filters funnel panel, "Add Filter" controls.
steps.why: A bounded open-lead queue keeps recurring reviews focused on actionable records.
steps.checkpoint: The Filters panel shows your open-status and date conditions, and the visible rows satisfy them.
hint_levels: Use status and recency to define what needs regular review.
Add a filter excluding your converted status and a Created Date or Last Modified Date range that matches your review cadence.
Click Filters > Add Filter > set Lead Status not equal to your converted status > Done, then Add Filter > choose Created Date or Last Modified Date > set the review range > Done > Save.

steps.action: Display the identity and ownership fields needed to spot future cleanup problems.
steps.where: Lead Cleanup Queue, List View Controls gear menu, "Select Fields to Display" dialog.
steps.why: Visible identity fields make duplicate and ownership problems easier to recognize during each review.
steps.checkpoint: The table visibly includes Lead Owner, First Name, Last Name, Company, Email, Phone, Lead Status, Created Date, and Last Modified Date.
hint_levels: Show the fields used to distinguish people and verify responsibility.
Add owner, contact identity, status, and audit-date fields, then place them in a useful order.

Click List View Controls > Select Fields to Display > move Lead Owner, First Name, Last Name, Company, Email, Phone, Lead Status, Created Date, and Last Modified Date to Visible Fields > reorder them > Save.

steps.action: Pin the Lead Cleanup Queue as the default Leads view.
steps.where: Pin icon beside the list view name at the top of the Leads page.
steps.why: Opening directly to the cleanup queue makes regular maintenance harder to overlook.
steps.checkpoint: The pin icon appears filled and "Lead Cleanup Queue" remains selected after reopening the Leads tab.
hint_levels: Look beside the view name for the pin.
Pinning makes the current list the default for the Leads object.
With Lead Cleanup Queue selected, click the pin icon beside its name.
